findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_prompt" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: The AI prompt of an UpFork component or landing page, as its page's copy button gives it: the whole code with instructions for bringing it into a project of any…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: my_articles, make_resume, support_inbox, read_ticket, update_article, open_ticket, my_tickets, answer_ticket · Private data: make_resume, read_product_file, view_product, read_article, open_ticket, install_product · Public sink: update_profile, reply_to_ticket, add_article_image, open_ticket, answer_ticket, publish_article · Destructive: delete_article, search_lessons, install_product.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: my_articles, make_resume, support_inbox, read_ticket, update_article, open_ticket, my_tickets, answer_ticket · Private data: make_resume, read_product_file, view_product, read_article, open_ticket, install_product · Public sink: update_profile, reply_to_ticket, add_article_image, open_ticket, answer_ticket, publish_article · Destructive: delete_article, search_lessons, install_product

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
